content: The drug naldapristin increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ranolazine increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting both the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Roxithromycin decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Rufinamide decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Sirolimus increases the levels or effects of estropipate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Estropipate decreases the effects of somapacitan by reducing the serum IGF-1 response to somapacitan. Patients may require higher somapacitan dosages. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Stiripentol affects estropipate by inhibiting and inducing the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Stiripentol also inhibits and induces the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring dosage adjustments for CYP3A4 substrates. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Estropipate decreases the effects of albiglutide by impairing glucose tolerance, potentially reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Glycemic control should be monitored in diabetic patients. Amikacin decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Estropipate decreases the effects of anastrozole by pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially diminishing the pharmacologic action of anastrozole. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced therapeutic efficacy. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of estropipate by inducing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used.
